# TABLE 1. --Summary of the principal water-bearing units underlying the Hollister and San Juan Valleys
AgeWater-bearing unitThickness (feet)Lithology and geologic formations includedOccurrence, structure, and hydrologic significance
River-channel deposits (Qrc)0-50(1)Unconsolidated sand and gravelOccur in channele of San Benito River and Tras Fines Creak. Contain water only in the western and of the San Juan Valley near the junction of the San Benito River with the Pajero River, and in . few reaches of Tree Pinos Creek only in the spring when ground-wa levels are highest. A minor aquifer. Should yield small to moderate quantities of water to welle. Allow large quantities of water to percolate downward into the underlying aquifers.
Alluvium (Qal)0-250(1) Unconsolidated lenticular beds of graval, sand, silt, and clay deposited by streams as flood- plain. alluvial-fan, slope-wash, and terrace deposits. May also include some lake beds. Includes Dos Picachos Gravels of Taliaferro [19461]Underliae the valley floors of the Bollister and San Juan Valleys and smaller tributary valleys. Flat lying. Cennot be distinquised from the underlying unite on driller's or electrical logs. May locally be dewetered. Probably is combined, in some areas, with underlying permeable onits to form a single hydrologic unit.
Older alluvium (QTal)UnknownUnconsolidated lenticular beds of gravel, sand, silt, and clay. Happed as San Benito Gravels by Taliaferro [1946?]Forms hilla along Calaveras fault from Bollister northward. Folded into small anticlinal structures. Subsurface distribution unknown.
San Benito Cravels of Lawson (1893) (QTeb)0-1,400Lenticular bads of gravel, send. and clay, locally consolidated into conglomerate, sandstone and clay-shale. Clays may contain occasional beds of impura lignite. Conglomerate contains material of aand to boulder size.Recognized in Hollister Valley only. Exposed at the surface mainly to the esst and southeast of Hollister. Probably occur in the subsurface beneath much of the central and western parts of the Hollistar Vallay. May consist of strata deposited by the ancestral San Benito River system. Moderately folded and faulted and rest with angular discordance upon the underlying older formations. Dips rarely exceed 25 degrees except nesr faults. Are a major aquifer in the Hollieter Valley. Probably act as a single hydrologic unit with the overlying alluvium. Yield moderate to large amounts of water to most wells.
Santa Clara Formation (QTac)UnknownCompact Ienticular beds of clay, sand, and gravel. Happed as San Benito Gravels by Taliaferro (1946?).Exposed in hills along Calaveres fault northwest of San Felipe Lake in Santa Clara County. fields small to moderate quantities of water to wells in Santa Clara County.
Upper member (Tpu)12,000- 3,000Predominantly friable, porous, light- gray, pebble gravel and sand. Well bedded, locally crossbedded. Pebbles well rounded, mostly of chert. quartzite, porphyry, granitic rocks, graywacke, and sandstone. Some heds contain cobbles. Contains some interbedded soft greenish- to reddish-gray siltstone in places. All terrestrial in origin. May be lithologic equivalent to San Benito Gravels of Lawson (1893)Recognized at the surface only in the Lomerias Musrtos and Flint Hills. Underlies the alluvium throughout much of the San Juan Valley. Extent beneath the alluvius in the area northeast of the Flint Hills and west of the Calaveras fault is unknown, but probably occurs mainly in the southern half of this area. Probably the major aquifer underlying the Sen Juan Valley Moderately folded and may be faulted in some areas. Locally contains water under artesian head. Yields moderate to large amounts of water to most wells.
Middle member (Tpm)14,000- 5,000Friable light-grey to greenish-gray bedded to massive sandstone, and interbedded green to locally reddish-gray gypsiferous clay. In placas contains friable pebbly sandstone or pebble conglomerate. In . few places unit contains fresh-water and brackish-water molluscan fossils. Whole unit is weakly consolidated and generally poorly exposed. Contact with underlying lower member gradationalDirectly underlies the alluvium in the southeastern part of the San Juan Valley. Folded and faulted and dipa as much as 90 degrees. Sand beds are more silty, finer grained, and compact than in the upper member and the alluvium and permeabilities are lower, Locally yields sufficient water for domestic and stock use. Locally contains water under moderately high artesian head. Water may contain large concentrations of sulfate locally. Probably contains salt water at depth throughout the area.
Lower member (Tpl)15,000- 7,000Mainly friable to semifriable, bedded, fine- to medium-grained arkosic sandstone and interbedded micaceous milstone. Sandstone is light gray, buff, and rusty yellow. In places some beda contain pebbles. Siltatone is light gray, weathers brownish gray; sandy argillaceous, micaceous, poorly bedded. Slightly fossiliferous Marine.Probably underlies the alluvius in the San Juan Valley only elong the northeast side of the San Andreas rift zone. Folded and faulted and dips as much as 90 degrees; locally overturned along San Andreas rift zone. Sand beda are probably less permeable, as a whole, than in middle member because of greater compaction. Information on well yields 1a lacking. May locally furnish sufficient watar for stock and domestic use. Contains salty water at shallow depths in some parts of the Lomerias Muertas. Probably contains water of poor chemical quality at depth throughout the area.
Unnamed unit 2 (Tu2)0-1,700Electrical and driller's logs indicate unit consists of from one to four thick-bedded sand or sandstone sequences with interbedded clay, shale, and siltstone. May contain some gravel and limestone.Not known to be exposed at surface. Beds may have moderate to steep dips toward center of valley. Not present west of Calaveras fault. Permeability 1a probably low.
Unnamed unit 1 (Tuj)0-1,100Electrical log of Dark, Garcia No. 1, located in sec. 30, T. 12 S., R. 6E., water-well driller's logs, and outcrops indicate unit consists of thick to medium heds of clay, silt, sand, and gravel. Character of unit in the subsurface may be different north of Fallon Road.Exposed in hills at northwest end of Santa Ana Valley. Beds may have moderate to steep dips toward center of valley. Not present west of Calaveras fault. Permeability is probably low.
Consolidated bedrock (TKJb)UnknownSedimentary, igneous, and metamorphic rocks. Includes Franciscan Formation, Panoche Formation, Indart Sandstone of Taliaferro [19467], Los Muertos Creek Formation of Wilson (1943), Tres Pinos Sandstone of Wilson (1943), Vaqueros Formation, Quien Sabe Volcanics of Tsliaferro [19467]. San Lorenzo Formation of Arnold (1906), Monterev Group, and Santa Lucia Granite of Lawson (1893)Crops out in the hills along the southeast, east and north sides of the Hollister Valley and in tbe bills on the west side of the San Andreas fault zone. Underlies the Bollieter and San Juan Vallevs at depth. Formations are highly folded and faulted. Rocks are dense and compact and yield only small quantities of water to wells from fractures, joints and weathered zones. May be a source of ground-water recharge to overlying water-bearing formations. Locally may contain water of poor chemical quality
